title: dynamic SLO stitcher and burst-tempering admission controller
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation:
Large tenants with spiky workloads can exhaust short-lived burst windows and then experience sustained throttles even when aggregate fleet capacity exists. This PR introduces a 'SLO stitcher' that synthesizes per-tenant short- and medium-window commitments into a single admission signal, and a burst-tempering admission controller that smooths admission decisions by accounting for recent debt and a configurable tempering coefficient.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a SLO stitcher component that consumes short-window (1m) and medium-window (10m) commitment/time-series and outputs a stitched target utilization plus a per-tenant debt estimate.
- Implements the burst-tempering admission controller that reduces immediate grant sizes based on debt and recent peak utilization to prevent repeated microbursts from starving other tenants.
- Adds telemetry beams for stitching decisions: headroom_heatmap, debt_ledger_events, and temperer_decision_samples. These are aggregated and exported via the existing metrics pipeline.
- Introduces a light-weight commit-budget ledger persisted in the runtime store (sharded by tenant) with expiry and reconciliation hooks for eventual consistency across controllers.
- Adds control-plane feature flags and YAML knobs for tempering_coefficient, stitch_window_ms, and debt_decay_half_life.

Design notes and rationale:
- We deliberately separate 'stitching' from admission so that other admission strategies (e.g. latency-first) can reuse the stitched SLO signal.
- Tempering is multiplicative and capped; we avoid hard rejects unless a tenant is over a hard debt_threshold. This preserves graceful degradation and fallbacks.
- Debt is tracked in a monotonic ledger; reconciliation runs periodically and clips negative drift.

Checklist:
- [x] Core SLO stitcher algorithm implemented and covered by unit tests
- [x] Admission controller wired into runtime admission path with feature-flag gating
- [x] Telemetry events, histograms, and dashboards (provisioned)
- [x] Config knobs and defaults documented
- [x] End-to-end test: multi-tenant spike scenario recreated in CI fixture and validated
- [x] Load testing in benchmark-lab showing <4% p95 latency regression at 500 tenants

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for ledger operations, stitch windows, and tempering math added under tests/autoscaler/.
- E2E scenario (e2e/fixtures/tenant_slo_test.yaml) simulates alternating 30s spikes for 20 tenants with overlapping peaks; validated that temperer reduces cross-tenant starvation by ~35% relative to baseline.
- Benchmarked under benchmark-lab: 500 tenants, bursty P95s show cost/latency tradeoff with tempering_coefficient=0.6 as default.

Migration notes:
- The ledger data is backward compatible. On deploy, the stitcher will start with empty ledgers and reconcile within a configured warmup window (default 5m).

Related work: ENG-1427 (SLO telemetry gaps), ENG-1489 (tenant grievance reduction), SUP-5342 (customer incident reproduced).

Docs: docs/design/slo-stitcher.md added with operational runbook and suggested dashboard panels.

discussion: Jordan Kim: Design LGTM overall. Couple of questions: 1) How does this interact with existing tenant warm pools? 2) Any latency on the admission path from stitcher calls?

Asha Patel: Reply: warm pools are upstream—stitcher only influences admission grants. We added an in-process cache for the stitched signal and use continuous batching to amortize compute; p99 additional admission latency measured <200us in bench profiles.
Sofia Nguyen: Please add a safety cap to prevent tempering from starving a tenant indefinitely (suggest max_temper_reduction).
Asha Patel: Added max_temper_reduction config and unit tests verifying it cannot drop grants below hard minimum.
release_notes: Introduce SLO stitcher and burst-tempering admission controller to smooth multi-tenant burst behavior. Adds telemetry (headroom_heatmap, debt_ledger_events) and config knobs. Default tempering coefficient=0.6. Operators should monitor headroom_heatmap and debt_ledger_events after upgrade.
notes_for_ops: Default warmup window = 5m; if migrating from very old clusters, set warmup window to 15m to allow ledgers to reconcile. Dashboard: console/dashboards/headroom_heatmap.json
observability_impacts: adds three new metrics streams: headroom_heatmap (histogram), debt_ledger_events (counter+labels), temperer_decision_samples (gauge samples)
rollback_plan: Disable feature flag 'slo_stitcher_enabled' and restart admission controller; ledger state is non-destructive and will be ignored when feature disabled.
